description: A fixed-length dataset whose record carries a table one of whose items is redefined, read noodoslide -- a constant three entries, the count an ordinary item beside them. Each entry is told apart by a kind byte sitting inside the entry itself, so the alternative is chosen once per occurrence and not once per record: both records here hold entries that do not all take the same arm, and a consumer that chose one arm for the record would read a foreign entry's country out of a domestic one's state and ZIP. The foreign arm is four bytes shorter than the run it redefines, so it carries a slack run no item covers, once per occurrence that takes it -- which rides the write-back half, since the arms a record's entries took decide how many such runs the record has and where they fall. ADR-TAIL is behind the table and holds the record's length to account: a dropped slack run, or a table read at the count rather than at the fixed three, moves it.
source: docs/ir/SPEC.md, "A variant is chosen once per occurrence", "A predicate on an arm reads one occurrence", "Members never overlap, and `REDEFINES` is resolved away", "Slack is a node, not a rule", "Slack survives a read" and "An item after a table slides, and the other reading is a fixed table"; docs/layout/SPEC.md, "A discriminator for a redefine inside a table", "The `OCCURS DEPENDING ON` reading is one statement per layout" and "lrecl and blksize describe the dataset, not the stream"; the alphanumeric bytes and the storage widths are cobol-go codec/SPEC.md, "Storage Widths" and "Group items, OCCURS, and SYNCHRONIZED". That the retained slack is the same bytes is not something a values document can state; see the corpus README.
